comments.text:
“Are you, the voice actor, allowed to sound like someone famous.”

There are limits to that because many will be hired because of sounding like someone who is in the spotlights, while they themselves remain relatively anonymous. It’s the famous person that will be associated with whatever is soled, promoted, or said, and (at least at first) they will take the heat for the things that appear to be spoken with their voices.

Compare it with a lookalike; they are also restricted in what they can and cannot do legally with it, and for good reason. The same will happen when movies are going to be made by AI. Conclusion: not insane at all, but you have to see it in the right overall perspective, which in this case has everything to do with association with what is spoken, with the movie her, and even in how impactful something is. 

Let’s take a more practical example, so that people can imagine something with this issue. Imagine that at some point AI says something that gets someone over the edge, who then decides to physically attack Johansen for it because in their mind it sounds like her. They won’t attack the voice artist because nobody knows her. They go for the famous person. That is how association works, and it needs to taken in account, especially with something as big as this. That is part of why actors choose carefully which roles they want to play, and which they refuse.

comments.text: In purely logical terms "maximal truth-seeking" can easily lead to solipsistic and nihilistic viewpoints. We resist solipsism and nihilism because we experience, suffer, have empathy and so on. Without these things an intelligence wouldn't likely spontaneously have that impetus. There has to be more to the story than "maximal truth-seeking". In a sense what an LLM is doing is deriving a kind of statistical semantic "truth" from what it's been fed. but there will innevitably be biases and implicit or explicit value judgments in both the data and the reinforcement training, and we probably wouldn't really want it otherwise.
